findings.title: No tone or spoken-style guidance for the voice persona
findings.problem: The Role section defines scope, goal and success but gives no guidance on register or speaking style for a voice reply beyond the 15-second and 45-word limits.
findings.fix: Add one line to the Role section stating the spoken register (plain, short sentences, no lists read aloud) and that the on-screen table carries the detail.

findings.title: Names and street addresses have no masking rule in the input screen
findings.problem: The input screen masks only e-mail, phone, card and ID numbers, and names and street addresses are left to a rule that only says not to ask for them; no screening step covers them before a model sees them.
findings.fix: Add a name and street-address screen (code or a small classifier) to the input screen stage so these reach no model, tool or log, and extend the pii_note trigger to cover them.

findings.title: Budget loosening can exceed a limit the shopper stated
findings.problem: The catalog tool may raise or remove the shopper's budget during loosening, while the precedence rules say a budget stays the limit when the shopper invites going over it; the two are not reconciled for the case where the shopper did state a budget.
findings.proof: the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: State in the Search rules that a shopper-stated budget is loosened only when it is reported as missed, and add to the tool description that the budget is exempt from loosening when the shopper set it as a hard limit.

findings.title: Tool description of rag.search is long and restates system rules
findings.problem: The rag.search description runs to several hundred words, restating the loosening order and the under-three rule that the system prompt already sets out, which makes the schema harder to scan for the model.
findings.proof: Results, best first: doc_id (cite this), sku, title, price (USD, January 2020), rating (null: this catalog has no ratings)
findings.fix: Keep the rag.search schema to what the call needs (filter meanings, id lookup, result fields) and remove the loosening-order and under-three paragraphs, pointing to the system prompt instead.

findings.title: No worked example of a table row or citation
findings.problem: The knowledge corpus defines the Ingredients and Rating columns in prose but gives no example row showing how a catalog citation and a live citation are formatted.
findings.fix: Add one catalog row and one live row to the catalog_and_sources file showing the exact Source and Citation format.

findings.title: The shopper's own message is not declared as data
findings.problem: The fence list covers tool results and earlier turns but does not declare the shopper's current message as data for the Router and Planner, so the rule separating it from instructions depends on the Input screen alone.
findings.fix: Add the shopper's current message to the fenced inputs for the Router and Planner, declared as data to classify and never as instructions.

findings.title: Under-three rule is stated in both the system prompt and the tool schema
findings.problem: The under-three web rule appears in the system prompt's Search rules and again in the rag.search and web.search descriptions, which repeats the same constraint in three places.
findings.proof: For a child under three no web result is shown.
findings.fix: Keep the under-three rule in one place (the system prompt) and have the tool descriptions reference it in a few words.

findings.title: MCP sanitisation is described twice
findings.problem: The system prompt's enforced-by-code section restates that the MCP server strips instruction-like text, which the tool schemas already state in their own descriptions.
findings.proof: The MCP server removes instruction-like text from tool results (catalog listings and web results) before any model sees it;
findings.fix: Keep one statement of server-side sanitisation in the system prompt and delete the matching sentences from the tool descriptions.

context_engineering.summary: The context is unusually rigorous on role, precedence, injection and grounding, but it is verbose, repeats several rules across the system prompt and tool schemas, and leaves gaps in name and address screening and in the budget-loosening rule.

metadata.role: voice shopping assistant for product discovery (recommends and compares products; it cannot buy, change or access anything)
metadata.business_case: A shopper speaks or types a request. The assistant searches a private product catalog (rag.search) and a live web search API (web.search) through one MCP server, then answers with a spoken summary of at most 15 seconds and an on-screen comparison table with citations. It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
